justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: No outcome studies for any AOTA specialty certification vs non-certified.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Portfolio and exam process; significant documentation and experience requirements.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicability varies by specialty (driving, feeding, low vision, school); each narrow but meaningful within its domain.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No billing impact for any AOTA specialty certification; professional signaling only.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited employer recognition; specialty areas have consistent but narrow demand.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Patients may prefer certified specialists in specific domains.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Specialty areas (driving, low vision, school-based, feeding) are mixed; driving/low-vision can be cash-pay; others rarely are.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Modest leverage in niche cash markets (e.g., driving rehab) but no broad premium-pricing power.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Recognizable within OT, but consumers don't shop by AOTA SCDCM/SCEM letters.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Could anchor a niche service line (driving rehab clinic) but the credential is individual, limiting scale.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Low direct-to-consumer awareness; referrals come from clinicians and case managers.
justifications.business.efficiency: Portfolio + experience requirements are nontrivial for a cert with modest business return.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Recognized by OT academia as legitimate specialty credentialing, though a tier below board certs.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Some scholarly reflection required; holders contribute to niche specialty literature.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Strong for faculty teaching specialty electives (driving, low vision, feeding, school-based).
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Variable by specialty; feeding and low vision have moderate evidence; others thinner.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Occasionally specified in OT faculty postings tied to specific curricular gaps.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Portfolio process is moderate burden; efficiency depends on specialty alignment with faculty role.
